rules.title: Just Cause Eviction Protections After 12 Months Occupancy
rules.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential property for 12 months, the owner cannot terminate tenancy without just cause, which must be stated in the written notice. Just cause includes specified at-fault and no-fault reasons.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to tenants who have continuously and lawfully occupied residential real property for 12 months or more, with special conditions if additional adult tenants are added before 24 months.
rules.exemptions: None specified in this section.
rules.quoted_span: after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.

rules.title: Limit on rent increases for residential real property
rules.requirement: An owner of residential real property shall not increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period, based on the lowest gross rental rate charged during the prior 12 months. Rent discounts, incentives, concessions, or credits accepted by the tenant are excluded from the calculation.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential real property in California, excluding certain exempt properties.
rules.exemptions: Exemptions include affordable housing restricted by deed or government agreement, dormitories owned by educational institutions, housing under stricter local rent control, housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the last 15 years (except mobilehomes), certain owner-occupied two-unit properties, and some mobilehome tenancies owned by non-corporate owners with required notice.
rules.interaction: Possible preemption of city rules; needs human review.
rules.quoted_span: (a) (1)   Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or u
rules.conflict_note: May preempt city rules: Berkeley Municipal Code section 13.76.110A; Rent Board Regulation 1148, Berkeley Rent Ordinance, Measure BB (2024), Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance, San Francisco Rent Ordinance, Admin. Code Chapter 37, https://www.sf.gov/news--annual-rent-increase-3126-22827-announced, Santa Ana Rent Stabilization Ordinance, Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance. The law allows local rent control ordinances that restrict annual increases to less than the state limits.

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482) Rent Increase Limits
rules.requirement: Annual rent increases are limited to 5% plus the regional cost of living increase, or 10%, whichever is lower, for buildings older than 15 years.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental units in California buildings older than 15 years, excluding certain exempt properties.
rules.exemptions: Exemptions include units constructed within the last 15 years, deed-restricted affordable housing, certain dormitories, two-unit properties with owner occupancy, and some single-family homes and condominiums under specific ownership and notification conditions.
rules.interaction: State law preempts the listed city rules.
rules.quoted_span: nnual rent increases are limited to no more than 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living for the region in which the property is located, or 10% whichever is lower).

rules.title: California Government Code Section 12955 - Housing Discrimination Prohibited
rules.requirement: It is unlawful for housing owners to discriminate or harass persons based on protected characteristics including source of income, and to use financial or income standards that fail to account for aggregate income of persons residing together equally. When government rent subsidies are involved, housing providers must base eligibility on the tenant's portion of rent and must offer applicants the option to provide alternative evidence of ability to pay instead of credit history, and consider such evidence reasonably.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all housing accommodations in California.
rules.exemptions: None stated.
rules.quoted_span:
(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.
(ii) If the applicant elects to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s
reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:
(I) Provide the applicant reasonable time to respond with that alternative evidence.
(II) Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.

rules.title: California Civil Code Section 1950.5 - Security Deposits for Residential Rental Agreements
rules.requirement: A landlord shall not demand or receive a security deposit in excess of one month's rent, except for certain conditions such as advance payment of six months' rent for leases of six months or longer, or up to two months' rent for small landlords with limited properties. The landlord must hold the security for the tenant and may only claim amounts reasonably necessary for specified purposes such as unpaid rent, damages beyond ordinary wear and tear, cleaning, and restoring personal property. The landlord must provide an itemized statement of deductions and return the remainder of the security within 21 days after the tenant vacates.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent (standard), up to 6 months advance rent, or 2 months for small landlords
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential rental agreements in California.
rules.exemptions: Exemptions include small landlords who are natural persons or LLCs with all natural person members owning no more than two rental properties with four or fewer units total, and certain provisions for service members.
rules.quoted_span: (c) (1) Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.

rules.title: Notification of Tenant Screening Fee Rights
rules.requirement: Owners or agents must provide a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and the maximum fee cap permitted under California law before receiving any screening fee.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential rental properties in Berkeley.
rules.quoted_span: When an owner or the owner’s agent gets a request to rent residential property in Berkeley from an applicant and the owner charges a fee to purchase a consumer credit report and to validate, review, or otherwise process an application, the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a c

rules.title: Prohibition of Non-Refundable Application Fees for Existing Tenants
rules.requirement: Owners or agents cannot charge a non-refundable fee to existing tenants for renewing a tenancy or for changes related to roommates in a pre-existing household.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential rental agreements in Berkeley.
rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.

rules.title: Eviction for lease breach requires unreasonable tenant behavior causing actual harm
rules.requirement: In any notice terminating a tenancy for a lease breach, the landlord must clearly describe the alleged breach, demonstrate that the tenant’s behavior was unreasonable, and show that the breach caused actual harm to the landlord. Eviction is not allowed for breaches that do not cause actual harm.
rules.coverage_conditions: Units fully or partially covered by Berkeley Rent Ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Units exempt from Rent Ordinance coverage including some government-subsidized units as specified by federal, state, or administrative law.
rules.quoted_span: In any notice terminating a tenancy for a lease breach, the landlord must clearly describe the alleged breach. The landlord must demonstrate that the tenant’s behavior was unreasonable, and may not evict tenants for lease breaches that do not cause the landlord any actual harm.

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
rules.requirement: Just cause eviction protections apply to most units in multifamily properties built before 1980 and single family homes with current tenancies that began before 1996, among others.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most units in multifamily properties built before 1980; single family homes with current tenancies that began before 1996; rooming houses with five or more rooms rented individually; partially covered for new construction after June 1980 and single-family homes with tenancy started on or after January 1, 1996; most condominiums; units with certain government subsidies.
rules.exemptions: Golden Duplex (owner-occupied duplex on Dec 31, 1979 with owner living in one unit); units where owner shares kitchen or bath with tenant and owner lived on property at tenancy start; tenancies started after Nov 7, 2018 on properties with ADU and owner-occupied unit; university rental units such as dormitories; nonprofit cooperatives.

rules.title: Relocation Assistance Payments for Owner Move-In and Ellis Act Evictions
rules.requirement: Owners must pay tenants relocation assistance in the event of an owner move-in eviction or Ellis Act eviction, with payments indexed annually to inflation.
rules.key_value: $19,413 standard payment; $6,471 additional payment for qualifying households (2026)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to owner move-in evictions and Ellis Act evictions in Berkeley.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance; Ellis Implementation Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance requires owners to pay tenants relocation assistance in the event of an owner move-in eviction. The Ellis Implementation Ordinance requires the same relocation assistance payments for tenants evicted so the owner can remove a property from the rental housing market. Both ordinances index the relocation payments to inflation, and provide that the Rent Board shall publish the yearly inflationary increases.

rules.title: Annual General Adjustment (AGA) for Year 2026
rules.requirement: Eligible landlords may increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than January 1, 2026, which is 65% of the CPI increase for the Bay Area from July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2025.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to eligible landlords and tenants with tenancy beginning before January 1, 2025, excluding those with rents set under Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act after that date.
rules.exemptions: Tenants whose tenancy began on or after January 1, 2025, with rents set pursuant to the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act are not subject to this increase.
rules.interaction: This city rule governs where it applies; the state rule yields to it (state rule is 'superseded').
rules.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code section 13.76.110A; Rent Board Regulation 1148
rules.quoted_span:
At its regular meeting on October 16, 2025, the Berkeley Rent Stabilization Board 
adopted the Annual General Adjustment (AGA) Order for Year 2026 which will allow 
eligible landlords to increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than 
January 1, 2026. The 2026 AGA of 1.0% represents 65% of the increase in the Consumer 
Price Index (CPI) for All Urban Consumers in the Bay Area during the period from July 1, 
2024 - June 30, 2025, which was 1.5% as posted by the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
rules.conflict_note: May be preempted by Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12. Needs human review.

rules.title: Annual General Adjustment capped at 5%
rules.requirement: The maximum Annual General Adjustment (AGA) for rent increases is capped at 5% per year, even if the formula based on the Consumer Price Index results in a higher percentage.
rules.coverage_conditions: Units fully covered by Berkeley Rent Ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Units partially covered or exempt from Rent Ordinance.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.
rules.conflict_note: May be preempted by Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12. Needs human review.

rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Rental housing providers in Berkeley are prohibited from inquiring about or using criminal history in rental advertising, applications, tenant selection, or decision-making. They cannot refuse to rent, terminate tenancy, demand higher deposits or rent, or disqualify tenants based on criminal history, with certain exemptions.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all rental housing providers in Berkeley except specified exemptions.
rules.exemptions: Exemptions include lifetime sex offenders, certain public housing/Section 8 properties, owner-occupied properties with 1-3 units where owner lives in one unit, units with rental agreements allowing owners to move back, and units occupied by existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.

rules.title: Utility charges must be included in base rent or separately metered and in tenant’s name
rules.requirement: For tenancies starting on or after February 6, 2024, landlords may charge tenants for utilities only if the cost is included in the base rent or if the utility is separately metered and the lease requires the tenant to place the utility account in their name.
rules.key_value: Utility charges included in rent or separately metered
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully covered rental units in Berkeley.
rules.exemptions: Units not fully covered by the Rent Ordinance or exempt units.
rules.quoted_span: For tenancies starting on or after February 6, 2024, a landlord may charge a tenant in a fully covered unit for utilities only if either: the cost of the  utilities are part of the base rent, or the utility service is separately-metered and the lease requires the tenant to place the utility in the tenant’s name.

rules.title: Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: The JCO prohibits termination of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions for most residential properties not regulated by the City's Rent Stabilization Ordinance.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles not regulated by the City's Rent Stabilization Ordinance, including buildings newer than October 1, 1978, and single-family dwellings.
rules.exemptions: Exemptions include transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner's roommate, certain cooperatives, some non-profit homeless facilities, short-term substance abuse treatment centers, and some government or HACLA-owned properties.
rules.interaction: This city rule governs where it applies; the state rule yields to it (state rule is 'superseded').
rules.citation: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.quoted_span:
If you own rental property in the City of Los Angeles, it may be subject to the
Just Cause Ordinance
(JCO).  It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.

rules.title: No-Fault Evictions Under the RSO & JCO
rules.requirement: All tenant not-at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and the filing of a Declaration of Intent to Evict form with the Los Angeles Housing Department before evicting tenants from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance or the Just Cause Ordinance. Notices to terminate tenancy can only be served after filing the Declaration, and a copy must be filed with LAHD no later than 3 days after service.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO) in Los Angeles.
rules.exemptions: Exemptions include evicting a resident manager to replace with another resident manager, evictions due to hazardous conditions caused by natural disasters not caused by landlord negligence, and certain other conditions.
rules.interaction: This city rule governs where it applies; the state rule yields to it (state rule is 'superseded').
rules.quoted_span:
All tenant not- at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and the filing of a 
Declaration of Intent to Evict form with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) before 
evicting tenants from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause 
Ordinance (JCO). Failure to file the Landlord Declaration with the LAHD makes the eviction a 
violation of the RSO or JCO.

rules.title: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) Just Cause Eviction
rules.requirement: Evictions under the RSO must be for legal reasons including tenant fault such as failure to pay rent or lease violations, or no-fault reasons such as owner or family move-in, demolition, government order, or conversion to affordable housing.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental properties in the City of Los Angeles subject to the Rent Stabilization Ordinance, generally those built on or before October 1, 1978.
rules.exemptions: Not specified in the text.
rules.interaction: This city rule governs where it applies; the state rule yields to it (state rule is 'superseded').
rules.quoted_span:
Legal Reasons for Eviction
Tenant is at-fault
Failure to pay rent
Failure to fix or address a violation of the rental agreement
Creating a nuisance or causing damage to the rental unit
Using the rental unit for an illegal purpose
Failure to renew a similar rental agreement
Failure to provide the landlord with reasonable access to the rental unit
The person at the end of the lease term is a subtenant not approved by the landlord
Tenant is not at-fault
The owner or immediate family member will move into the rental unit
A resident manager will move into the rental unit
Demolition and permanent removal from the rental market
Government order
Conversion to affordable housing

rules.title: Relocation Assistance and Tenant Protections for Demolition for New Construction under Resident Protections Ordinance
rules.requirement: A landlord terminating tenancy to demolish a Protected Unit for new construction must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict or Notice of Intent to Withdraw with LAHD, serve written notice to tenants, and pay relocation assistance per State or City law, whichever is higher, including enhanced amounts for lower income tenants under the Resident Protections Ordinance effective 2/11/2025.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to Protected Units that are residential dwelling units subject to rent or price control or rented by lower income households within the past five years, or withdrawn under Ellis Act within past 10 years.
rules.exemptions: Units that are not Protected Units or not occupied by lower income tenants follow regular RSO or JCO relocation rules.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Municipal Code Sections 151.22-151.28, 165.03.I(1); Ordinances #188481 and #188482
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord terminating a tenancy to demolish for new construction is required to pay relocation 
assistance and to file a Declaration of Intent to Evict or Notice of Intent to Withdraw Units From Rental 
Housing Use with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) prior to evicting tenants from units 
covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO).

rules.title: Relocation Assistance Payment Amounts for No-Fault Evictions
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay relocation assistance to tenants displaced by no-fault evictions. The amount depends on tenant status (qualified or eligible), length of tenancy, income, and property type, with specific amounts set annually.

rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to tenants displaced by no-fault evictions under the Rent Stabilization Ordinance or Just Cause Ordinance in Los Angeles.
rules.exemptions: Reduced relocation payments apply for 'Mom and Pop' properties under certain conditions and for single-family dwellings owned by natural persons under the JCO.

rules.title: Relocation Assistance Payment Requirements
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay relocation assistance to tenants within 15 days of serving a notice to terminate tenancy, with amounts set by RSO, JCO, or State Housing Crisis Act, whichever is higher, and enhanced for lower income tenants under the Resident Protections Ordinance.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to tenants of units covered by RSO, JCO, or State Housing Crisis Act, especially lower income tenants under the Resident Protections Ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Not applicable to units that are not Protected Units or not occupied by lower income tenants, which follow regular RSO or JCO rules.

laws require all tenants be paid relocation assistance in the amounts required by the RSO or JCO

rules.requirement: Landlords must pay interest on security deposits held under the RSO.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental properties in the City of Los Angeles subject to the Rent Stabilization Ordinance, generally those built on or before October 1, 1978.
rules.exemptions: Not specified in the text.

rules.title: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing Ordinance
rules.requirement: The sale, licensing, and use of algorithmic devices that use or incorporate nonpublic competitor data to advise or recommend rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental properties are prohibited in the City of San Diego.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential rental properties in the City of San Diego using algorithmic devices as defined.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to software that publishes reports using publicly available aggregated data or software used to set rents or income limits under affordable housing program guidelines.
rules.citation: San Diego Municipal Code Chapter 9, Article 8, Division 11, Sections 98.1101-98.1104
rules.quoted_span:
The proposed ordinance bans the sale, licensing, and use of an algorithmic device to set rental rates or 
occupancy levels for residential rental properties. Algorithmic devices are a software or product that uses 
or incorporates one or more algorithms to perform calculations of nonpublic competitor data concerning 
rental rates, occupancy levels, or other information regarding the leasing of residential rental property to 
advise, or recommend to a landlord, rental rates or occupancy levels.

rules.title: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing
rules.requirement: It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an algorithmic device to a landlord. It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential rental properties in the City of San Diego.
rules.exemptions: Algorithmic devices used only to publish reports from historical data older than 90 days or public information, and devices used to set rental rates or income limits under affordable housing program guidelines are exempt.
rules.quoted_span:
(a) It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an
algorithmic device to a landlord.
(b) It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates
or occupancy levels for residential rental property.

rules.title: Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy
rules.requirement: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which includes both at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause as defined in the ordinance.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental properties except those exempted under section 98.0703.
rules.exemptions: Exemptions include transient and tourist hotel occupancy, short-term residential occupancy, deed-restricted affordable housing, mobilehomes under Mobilehome Residency Law, nonprofit transitional housing, dormitories owned by educational institutions, landlord-occupied units with shared facilities, single-family residences occupied by the landlord with limited rented rooms, properties with certificate of occupancy issued within last 15 years (except mobilehomes), and certain owner-occupied properties not owned by corporations or REITs.
rules.interaction: This city rule governs where it applies; the state rule yields to it (state rule is 'superseded').
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this 
Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.

rules.title: Prohibition on algorithmic devices to set rents
rules.requirement: The sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units is prohibited in San Francisco.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential rental units in San Francisco.
rules.exemptions: No exemptions stated.
rules.quoted_span: The law prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco.

rules.title: Just Cause Eviction Reasons under San Francisco Rent Ordinance Section 37.9(a)
rules.requirement: A landlord must have a just cause reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing eviction from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance. There are 17 specified just cause reasons including non-payment of rent, substantial lease breach, nuisance, illegal use, refusal to renew lease, refusal to allow landlord access, unauthorized subtenant, owner-occupancy, condominium conversion, demolition, capital improvements, substantial rehabilitation, Ellis Act withdrawal, lead remediation, development agreements, Good Samaritan tenancy expiration, and development project demolition.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental units covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance, including some units exempt from rent increase limits but still subject to eviction provisions.
rules.exemptions: Tenancies in newly constructed rental units with Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979, tenancies eligible under Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act, and some rent-regulated tenancies by other agencies are exempt from rent increase limits but still subject to just cause eviction provisions.
rules.interaction: This city rule governs where it applies; the state rule yields to it (state rule is 'superseded').
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction. Note that the mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not constitute "just cause" for eviction.

rules.title: Relocation Payments for Evictions based on Owner/Relative Move-in, Demolition, Capital Improvement, or Substantial Rehabilitation
rules.requirement: Tenants evicted due to owner or relative move-in, demolition, permanent removal of unit from housing use, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation are entitled to relocation payments as specified by the Rent Board.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to evictions based on owner/relative move-in, demolition, permanent removal of unit from housing use, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation.
rules.exemptions: Temporary capital improvement evictions for less than 20 days are governed by California Civil Code Section 1947.9 and not by Rent Ordinance Section 37.9C.
rules.quoted_span: Relocation Payments for Evictions based on Owner/Relative Move-in OR Demolition/Permanent Removal of Unit from Housing Use OR Temporary Capital Improvement Work* OR Substantial Rehabilitation

rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental units covered by San Francisco rent control ordinances.
rules.exemptions: Certain units may be exempt under San Francisco rent control laws, such as new construction or owner-occupied units.

rules.quoted_span: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.
rules.conflict_note: May be preempted by Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12. Needs human review.

rules.title: Security Deposit Interest Rate for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027
rules.requirement: Security deposits must accrue interest at a rate of 4.2% for the period March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to security deposits held on rental units covered by San Francisco rent control ordinances.
rules.exemptions: Certain exemptions may apply under San Francisco rent control laws.
rules.interaction: This city rule governs where it applies; the state rule yields to it (state rule is 'superseded').
rules.citation: San Francisco Rent Ordinance, Admin. Code Chapter 37
rules.quoted_span:
Security Deposit Interest:
4.2% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027

rules.title: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.requirement: After 30 days of tenancy, an owner shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which must be stated in a written notice. Just cause includes certain at-fault and no-fault reasons such as nonpayment of rent, lease breaches, nuisance, criminal activity, owner occupancy, removal from rental market, demolition, or substantial remodel.
rules.coverage_conditions: Does not apply to housing produced in the last 15 years, deed-restricted affordable housing, hotels, hospitals, dormitories, and other shared living quarters.
rules.exemptions: Exemptions include housing built in the last 15 years, deed-restricted affordable housing, hotels, transient occupancy, hospital and care facilities, dormitories, and other shared living quarters.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span:
After 30 days, an owner shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in a written notice.
“Just cause” includes certain at-fault causes such as default in payment of rent, breach of a material term of the lease, committing a nuisance, criminal activity, and other actions.
“Just cause” also includes certain no-fault causes such as the intent of the owner to occupy the property, removal of the property from the rental market, and demolition or substantial remodel.

rules.title: Just Cause Eviction Requirement
rules.requirement: Landlords must have a valid reason such as nonpayment of rent, lease violation, or landlord move-in to evict tenants.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental units covered by the Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Not stated in the text.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Your landlord must have a valid reason to evict you. This could be for not paying rent, breaking the lease, or if the landlord wants to move into the property themselves.

rules.title: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization Ordinance
rules.requirement: Residential rent increases are limited to the lower of 3% per year or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period. If the CPI is negative, no rent increase is permitted.
rules.key_value: 3% per year or 80% of CPI change, whichever is lower
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental properties except buildings constructed after February 1, 1995, and mobile home spaces rented after January 1, 1990.
rules.exemptions: Exemptions for residential buildings constructed after February 1, 1995, and mobile home spaces rented after January 1, 1990.
rules.quoted_span: Increase in residential rents are limited to the lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period. If the CPI is negative, no rent increase is permitted.
rules.conflict_note: May be preempted by Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12. Needs human review.

rules.title: Maximum Allowable Rent Increase
rules.requirement: The landlord can only raise rent by the lesser of 3% of the current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change each year.
rules.key_value: 3% or 80% of CPI, whichever is less
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental units covered by the Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Not stated in the text.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The increase cannot be more than 3% of your current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change, whichever is less.
rules.conflict_note: May be preempted by Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12. Needs human review.

rules.title: An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting
rules.requirement: This act prohibits the use of algorithmic rent setting in the rental housing market in Massachusetts.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all rental housing in Massachusetts.
rules.quoted_span: An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting

rules.title: General Law - Part II, Title I, Chapter 186, Section 11
rules.requirement: A landlord may terminate a lease for nonpayment of rent by giving fourteen days' written notice to quit. The tenant can avoid termination by paying all rent due, with interest and costs, before the answer is due in a possession action. If nonpayment is due to delayed government payments, the court must continue the hearing at least seven days and treat the tenancy as not terminated if rent is tendered within that time.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to leases with written rent agreements in Massachusetts.
rules.quoted_span: Upon the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due under a written lease, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease, unless the tenant, on or before the day the answer is due, in an action by the landlord to recover possession of the premises, pays or tenders to the landlord or to his attorney all rent then due, with interest and costs of suit.

rules.title: Notice to quit for nonpayment of rent must include specific information and form
rules.requirement: A notice to quit for nonpayment of rent must be accompanied by a form including documentation of repayment agreements and information on rental assistance programs, court rules, and eviction restrictions. Courts shall not accept eviction filings without proof of delivery of this form.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential tenants receiving notice to quit for nonpayment of rent.
rules.quoted_span: No court having jurisdiction over an action for summary process pursuant to chapter 239, including the Boston municipal court department, shall, in an eviction for nonpayment of rent for a residential dwelling unit, accept for filing a writ, summons or complaint without proof of delivery of the form required under this section.

rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act
rules.requirement: Landlords planning to end a tenancy must provide tenants with a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources at the same time as the Notice to Quit or Notice of Lease Non-renewal. This notice must also be provided to tenants asked to leave due to property foreclosure or sale.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all landlords and foreclosing owners ending tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy in Boston, except residences in hospitals, skilled nursing or health facilities, and non-profit short-term treatment facilities for substance abuse.
rules.exemptions: Residences in hospitals, skilled nursing or health facilities, and non-profit short-term treatment facilities for substance abuse are exempt.
rules.citation: Boston Housing Stability Notification Act, Sec. 10-11.7
rules.quoted_span:
The HSNA requires that landlords give this Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources
to tenants when the landlord starts the eviction process, or when the landlord
decides to not offer the tenant a renewal of their lease agreement.

rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act
rules.requirement: All landlords planning to end a tenancy agreement must provide the tenant with a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources at the same time as the Notice to quit or Notice of non-renewal of lease. Landlords must also submit tenant contact information and a copy of the Notice to Quit or Notice of Non-renewal of Lease to the city using an online form.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all landlords planning to end a tenancy agreement in the City of Boston.
rules.quoted_span:
The Housing Stability Notification Act requires
ALL LANDLORDS
planning to end a tenancy agreement to provide the tenant with a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources.

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
rules.requirement: Housing providers receiving DND funding or with income restricted units under BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy must not impose blanket denials based on arrests or convictions and must consider applicants on a case-by-case basis. Arrests without conviction, juvenile records, convictions subject to judicial relief, and convictions older than 5 years generally cannot be considered unless there is a direct relationship to housing safety risk.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development funding and/or land, or with income restricted units created under Boston Planning and Development Agency Inclusionary Development Policy.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply where federal or state law imposes conflicting criminal history requirements; also does not apply to current criminal behavior or where there is a direct relationship between conviction and housing safety risk.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy, Department of Neighborhood Development, February 2017
rules.quoted_span:
Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or 
land, or that have income restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development 
Agency (BPDA) Inclusionary Development Policy will not impose a blanket policy that denies 
housing to anyone with arrests and or convictions. Housing providers will consider applicants on 
a case-by-case basis.

rules.title: Tenants Rights and Resources Notification Ordinance, Chapter 8.71
rules.requirement: Landlords must provide tenants with a guide about tenants' rights and resources at the start of tenancy and when tenancy is being terminated, including when legal steps to terminate tenancy are taken.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential rental agreements including single residential dwelling units in Cambridge, MA.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to rental units in hospitals, skilled nursing or health facilities, non-profit short-term treatment facilities for substance abuse, or Short Term Rental Units as defined in Cambridge Zoning Ordinance Article 4, Section 4.60.
rules.quoted_span: The Ordinance requires owners, landlords, and management companies to provide you with information at the start of your lease or tenancy as well as when your tenancy is being terminated.

rules.title: Residential rental property application fee not to exceed $50
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent shall not require an application or similar fee to apply to lease or sublease residential rental property for dwelling purposes exceeding $50, adjusted annually by CPI.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental properties except one-family or two-family dwellings and licensees of the NJ Real Estate Commission who are not landlords.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to dwelling units in one-family or two-family dwellings or to licensees of the NJ Real Estate Commission unless they are landlords.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord, or
agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply
to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which
exceeds $50.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act - Grounds for Eviction
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict a tenant only for good cause as specified by statute, including failure to pay rent, disorderly conduct, damage to property, substantial violation of lease rules, breach of lease covenants, and failure to pay rent increase after notice.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rental properties including single-family homes, mobile homes, apartments, rooming and boarding homes.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units, hotels, motels, or transient/seasonal guests renting less than 120 days, or units held in trust for developmentally disabled family members.
rules.quoted_span:
No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a 
lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause. The landlord must be able to 
prove in court that he has grounds for an eviction.

rules.title: Eviction for Permanent Retirement of Property from Residential Use
rules.requirement: If a landlord wants to permanently retire a building or mobile home park from residential use (not covered by health and safety removal), they must serve a Notice to Quit at least 18 months before filing suit for eviction and cannot take legal action until the lease expires.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies when landlord wants to permanently retire property from residential use, excluding health and safety removal cases.
rules.exemptions: None stated.
rules.quoted_span:
If the landlord wants to permanently retire a building or mobile home park from residential 
use, provided the circumstances covered under section (G) above do not apply, the landlord 
may file suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least 18 months 
prior to filing the suit for eviction. No legal action may be taken until the lease expires  
(N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(h)).

rules.title: Eviction for Continuous Failure to Pay Rent or Habitual Late Payment
rules.requirement: If a tenant continuously fails to pay rent or habitually pays late after a written Notice to Cease, the landlord may file suit for eviction with at least one month Notice to Quit.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies when tenant habitually pays rent late or fails to pay after written Notice to Cease.
rules.exemptions: None stated.
rules.quoted_span:
If the tenant continuously fails to pay rent or habitually pays late, after written Notice to 
Cease, the landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the 
tenant at least one month before filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(j)).

rules.title: Eviction for Termination of Employment-Based Tenancy
rules.requirement: If a tenant resides on the condition of employment by the landlord and that employment is terminated, the landlord may file suit for eviction with a Notice to Quit served three days prior to filing.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to tenants residing on condition of employment by landlord as superintendent, janitor, or similar.
rules.exemptions: None stated.
rules.quoted_span:
If a tenant resides in the property on the condition that, he is employed by the landlord as 
a superintendent, janitor, or in some other job and that employment is terminated the 
landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant three 
days prior to filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(m)).

rules.title: Eviction for criminal convictions and related conduct
rules.requirement: A landlord may file for eviction if the tenant or a person permitted by the tenant has been convicted of certain crimes including drug offenses, theft, or human trafficking related to the premises. No eviction suit may be brought more than two years after the conviction or related event.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to tenants convicted of drug offenses, theft, or human trafficking related to the premises or allowing such persons to reside there.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to tenants allowing juveniles found delinquent for drug use or possession to reside at the property.
rules.quoted_span:
No eviction suit may 
be brought more than two years after : the juvenile was found to be delinquent; 
conviction of the person; or after the person’s release fr om incarceration, whichever is 
later. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing suit 
for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(p)).

rules.title: Prohibition on landlord reprisal evictions
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot evict, substantially alter lease terms, or refuse to renew a lease in retaliation for a tenant exercising certain civil rights such as enforcing lease or law rights, making good faith complaints, or organizing tenants.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all rental properties except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings.
rules.exemptions: Excludes owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord cannot take reprisal action against a tenant by eviction, substantial alteration of 
a lease or its terms, or refusal to renew a lease when a tenant exercises certain civil rights (N.J.S.A. 
2A:42-10.10).  The law against reprisal applies to all rental properties used for dwelling purposes, 
including mobile homes, except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings.

rules.title: Eviction allowed after successful appeal overturning discrimination finding
rules.requirement: If a housing provider successfully appeals a director's decision finding a violation of the act and the court overturns the decision, the housing provider may evict the former applicant residing in the unit with at least 45 days' notice.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies when a housing provider successfully appeals a director's decision under this act and the tenant resides in the unit as a result of that decision.
rules.quoted_span:
if an appeal by a
housing provider is successful, and the court overturns a final decision of the
director that resulted in an order under this paragraph, then a determination
that the housing provider did not violate the provisions of this act as evidenced
by such successful appeal shall be grounds for the housing provider to evict
the former applicant if that person resides in a rental dwelling unit owned by
the housing provider as the result of the director’s order, so long as the
housing provider provides the applicant with at least 45 days’ notice prior to
the eviction

rules.title: Lease Termination for Disabled Tenants
rules.requirement: A disabled tenant may terminate the lease if the unit is not handicapped accessible and the landlord refuses or is unable to make the unit accessible after request.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to tenants with disabilities requesting accessibility modifications.
rules.exemptions: None stated.
rules.quoted_span:
New Jersey State Law also allows a disabled tenant to terminate the lease agreement if the 
unit is not handicapped accessible. A lease can be terminated if the landlord refuses to make the 
unit handicapped accessible after the tenant requests that the unit be made handicapped accessible 
and the landlord is unable or unwilling to do so

rules.title: Lease Termination Due to Domestic Violence
rules.requirement: Victims of domestic violence may terminate their lease without penalty prior to the expiration of the lease by providing the landlord with written notice and specified documentation. Lease termination takes effect on the 30th day following landlord's receipt of notice and documentation, with rent prorated up to termination date.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential leases except transient or seasonal rentals.
rules.exemptions: Transient or seasonal rentals are exempt.
rules.quoted_span:
victims of domestic violence may terminate their 
lease without penalty prior to the expiration of  the lease by providing the landlord with a 
written notice that the tenant or a child of the tenant faces an imminent threat of serious 
physical harm from a specific person, (that must be identified in the written notice) , if the 
tenant remains on the premises, and by fulfilling any of the following requirements

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act rent increase limits
rules.requirement: Before an owner can evict a tenant for nonpayment of an increased rent, they must serve a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase. The rent increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.
rules.key_value: rent increase must not be unconscionable
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all rental properties subject to eviction and rent increase laws in New Jersey.
rules.exemptions: Publicly financed and subsidized housing developments owned or subsidized by HUD or NJHMFA are not subject to municipal rent control ordinances.
rules.quoted_span:
before an owner can evict a tenant for nonpayment of 
an increased rent, they must first serve the tenant with a valid notice to quit and notice of rent 
increase. This notice does not mean that the tenant must actually leave; the tenant has the right to 
remain as long as they pay any legal increase in rent. The increase in rent must not be 
unconscionable; it must not be so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest 
person and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Limitations on Consideration of Criminal Records
rules.requirement: A housing provider shall not evaluate an applicant based on arrests not resulting in conviction, expunged convictions, pardoned convictions, vacated convictions, juvenile adjudications, or sealed records. After a conditional offer, only certain recent or serious convictions may be considered.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental dwelling units other than owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are exempt.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Prohibition on Discriminatory Advertising
rules.requirement: A housing provider shall not knowingly publish any advertisement that excludes applicants based on criminal records except for specific drug-related and sex offender registration cases. They also shall not use or distribute criminal records inconsistently with the Act.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental dwelling units other than owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are exempt.
rules.quoted_span:
A housing provider shall not knowingly or
purposefully publish, or cause to be published, any housing advertisement that
explicitly provides that the housing provider will not consider any applicant
who has been arrested or convicted of one or more crimes or offenses, except
for
drug-related criminal activity for the
manufacture or production of methamphetamine on the premises of federally
assisted housing, and whether the applicant is subject to a lifetime
registration requirement under a State sex offender registration program.

rules.title: Prohibition on requiring drug or alcohol tests or drug abuse treatment information
rules.requirement: A housing provider shall not require an applicant to submit to a drug or alcohol test, or request the applicant’s consent to obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all housing providers and applicants in New Jersey.
rules.quoted_span:
A housing provider shall not require an applicant
to submit to a drug or alcohol test, or request the applicant’s consent to
obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.

rules.title: Return of Security Deposit After Lease Termination Due to Domestic Violence
rules.requirement: Within 15 business days after lease termination due to domestic violence, the landlord must make the security deposit plus any interest available to the tenant or agent, and notify the tenant in writing within 3 business days when and where to pick it up. The deposit must be available for 30 days during normal business hours.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies when lease is terminated under the Safe Housing Act due to domestic violence.
rules.exemptions: None stated.
rules.quoted_span:
Within 15 business days after the lease  is terminated, the landlord shall make available 
the return of the tenant’s security deposit, plus any interest earned, to the tenant or the tenant’s 
agent. In addition, within three business days after the lease is terminated, the landlord must notify 
the tenant in writing of when and where the tenant can pick up the security deposit.

rules.title: Truth in Renting Act Security Deposit Requirements
rules.requirement: Landlords must comply with New Jersey statutes regarding security deposits, including disclosure and handling requirements.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental dwelling units in New Jersey.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to hotels, motels, or other guest houses serving transient or seasonal tenants.
rules.quoted_span:
Every landlord subject to the Truth in Renting Act, (N.J.S.A. 46:8-43 to 51), hereinafter 
the Act, is required to distribute one copy of the Truth in Renting Statement to each of their tenants 
within 30 days after it has been posted by the Department on its website and shall thereafter provide 
a copy of the most current statement to each new tenant at or prior to the time the tenant executes 
a lease for the rental unit.
